findings.title: Accidental git submodule (gitlink) committed
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink pointing at the base commit (a5d29095…). It is unrelated to the feature and looks like a local checkout of the repo that got staged by mistake. Merging it adds a broken or recursive submodule entry to the repository, with no `.gitmodules` entry to back it. Remove it from the PR.

findings.title: Substring check treats negated or other error-type filters as error-focused
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever `"event.type:error"` appears anywhere in the lowercased query string. A query like `!event.type:error` (which excludes errors) contains that substring, so it is treated as error-focused. So is `event.type:errors_foo`. For allowlisted projects on the discover dataset, `count()` is then rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` for non-error events, which have no sample_weight. The result is wrong counts, usually 0. Parse the query, or at least reject negated filters.

findings.title: Upsampling decision ignores the dataset and query actually being executed
Eligibility cache is never invalidated and contradicts its own documentation
findings.body: Eligibility is cached for 60s per org and project set. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called, even though its docstring says it should run when the allowlist changes. As a result, allowlist changes take up to 60s to apply, and different hosts can return different counts for the same query in that window. The docstring on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` also claims the configuration is read fresh each time, which the cache makes false. Either wire up invalidation or drop the cache.

findings.title: Cache adds a remote round-trip in front of an already-cached option lookup
findings.body: The code claims `options.get` is an expensive lookup. In practice options are cached in-process, so `options.get` is cheap. Putting `cache.get` / `cache.set` in front of it adds a memcached or redis round-trip to every `_get_event_stats` call, which makes the request slower rather than faster. The key is also built from Python `hash()` of the project tuple, so two different project sets can collide and share an eligibility result.

findings.title: upsampled_count silently drops events without sample_weight
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no fallback. Events that have no sample_weight contribute nothing to the sum. That includes events ingested before a project was allowlisted, or events whose SDK sent no client sample rate. Once a project is allowlisted, historical or unsampled error counts drop toward 0 instead of counting as 1 each. Use something like `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))`. The result type is also declared `number` while `count()` is `integer`, which changes the response meta for the same yAxis.
